anomalies.observed: The net /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW contains only the anodes of D14, D23, and D4, with no connection to any power source or driver.
anomalies.expected: The LED anodes should be tied to a 3.3V power rail (e.g., +3V3) so the LEDs can illuminate when their cathodes are pulled low by the CM4 or buffers.
anomalies.impact: Ethernet link/activity LEDs D14, D23 and activity LED D4 will never light because their anodes are floating.

anomalies.observed: D30 pin 4 (A2) is on ESTOP_OUT, and pin 2 (K2) connects through R60 to the same ESTOP_OUT net, so the second LED of D30 is between ESTOP_OUT and ESTOP_OUT.
anomalies.expected: The cathode of the e-stop indicator LED (D30 pin 2) should return to GND through R60 (as pin 1 does through R59 to GND), so the LED lights when ESTOP_OUT is active.
anomalies.impact: The second LED of D30 (likely the e-stop indicator) will never illuminate, so the e-stop status indication is lost.

anomalies.observed: Both GND1 (logic side) and GND2 (bus side) of the isolated CAN transceivers U10 and U11 are connected to the common GND net. Their VCC2 pins are powered from the non-isolated 5V_switched_CAN rail.
anomalies.expected: For isolated CAN buses, GND1 and GND2 must be on separate isolated ground nets, and VCC2 must be supplied by an isolated DC-DC converter.

evidence.quote: GND [High Power] : ... U10.4(GND1,power_in) U10.5(GND2,power_in) U11.4(GND1,power_in) U11.5(GND2,power_in) ...
two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (U8, U9) through an isolated CAN transceiver (U11/companion)

anomalies.impact: The galvanic isolation of the CAN buses is defeated, allowing ground loops and common-mode noise between the robot's logic and motor controllers, contrary to the intended isolated design.

parsed.summary: The design files contain multiple deviations: three LED anodes are left floating on /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW, the e-stop indicator LED D30 is shorted out by connecting its cathode resistor to ESTOP_OUT instead of GND, and the isolated CAN transceivers have their logic and bus grounds tied together, defeating isolation.
